primitives.name: Provenance Chain Integrity
primitives.verbatim_quote: For a sports intelligence platform, provenance is not optional — it is the structural foundation of the trust model.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C': 'Claim object, dimensionless', 'S': 'Source object, dimensionless', 'T': 'Trust score, [0,1]', 'E': 'Evidence chain, ordered set'}
primitives.assumptions: Each claim C must have a unique path E → S such that T(E,S) > threshold.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ∃C s.t. ∀E, ∄S such that T(E,S) ≥ threshold.

layer2.mapping: Chain of evidence E maps to Bayesian likelihood P(C|E), where trust T = P(C|E) × P(E|S)

primitives.name: Tier 1 Review Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: Win rate claim check (requires ≥30 settled picks, defined window, model version) 3.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R': 'Review status, {approved, rejected}', 'W': 'Win rate, [0,1]', 'N': 'Number of picks, integer', 'M': 'Model version, string'}
primitives.assumptions: A claim with win rate W requires N ≥ 30 picks over time window Δt with model M.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When N < 30 or Δt < defined window or M ≠ current version.

layer2.mapping: Kernel function K(R,W,N,M) = 1 if all constraints met else 0; used in GSE state transition logic

primitives.name: Failure Mitigation Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: Accuracy about what was claimed and what happened matters for the trust model.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F': 'Failure event, boolean', 'P': 'Published claim, dimensionless', 'A': 'Audit trail, ordered list', 'V': 'Voided pick, boolean'}
primitives.assumptions: If F occurs, then P must be corrected or removed and A updated accordingly.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F ∧ ¬(P ∈ A) or V = true but P still visible.

layer2.mapping: Failure event F maps to correction protocol: P ← P_corrected ∨ P ← void, A ← A ∪ F_log

The 'failure_mitigation' protocol ensures retroactive consistency by enforcing that any detected inconsistency F triggers a correction or voiding mechanism. These primitives form a closed-loop system: claims are validated, reviewed, and corrected if necessary, maintaining a consistent audit trail A that supports both GSI's probabilistic inference and GSE's state transitions.
